1. Real authentication added: ASP.NET Core Identity with Login, Remember Me, Forgot Password.
2. Impersonation removed entirely — replaced by real login.
3. Three Identity roles: HR, DepartmentHead, Employee.
4. Separate ApplicationUser table (extends IdentityUser<int>) with FK → Employees(Id).
5. HR creates both Employee record and ApplicationUser account in one transaction.
6. DepartmentHead is now both an Identity role AND a data relationship (Department.ManagerId).
7. Manager replacement now also reassigns the DepartmentHead Identity role (same transaction).
8. Authorization: Area-level via [Authorize(Roles=...)] on base controllers.

9. ICurrentUserService now reads from ClaimsPrincipal, not session. 10. IsPasswordChangeRequired flag added to ApplicationUser — HR-created accounts must change password on first login. 11. ProcessedBy on Payroll changed to NOT NULL (always set by HR). 12. RejectionReason column added to LeaveRequests. 13. IsDeleted column added to Attendances for cascade on employee soft-delete. 14. DepartmentHead blocked from approving their own leave (FR12 updated). 15. TaskAssignmentPolicy: AssignedById != AssignedToId (self-assignment blocked). 16. Overdue task definition added to Section 8.7. 17. NFR07–NFR09 added: HTTPS/HSTS, pagination, and WCAG 2.1 Level A accessibility.
The HR system is built on the following immutable principles:
Real authentication via ASP.NET Core Identity – email + password, Remember Me, Forgot Password.
Three Identity roles: HR, DepartmentHead, and Employee.
Department manager is both a data relationship (Department.ManagerId) AND an Identity role (DepartmentHead) – they must always stay in sync.
Every department must have exactly one manager – a non-HR, active, non-deleted Employee in the same department who also holds the DepartmentHead role.
Only DepartmentHeads can assign tasks – HR cannot assign tasks.
Managers cannot be deleted without replacement – HR must assign a new manager first.
Manager replacement is a single transaction that does four things:

(1) update Department.ManagerId, (2) remove DepartmentHead role from old manager's ApplicationUser, (3) add DepartmentHead role to new manager's ApplicationUser, (4) optionally proceed with deletion of original manager.

When an employee is soft-deleted, ALL tasks they appear in are also soft-deleted – both tasks they created (AssignedById) and tasks assigned to them (AssignedToId). Silent cascade. Tasks are NOT restored if the employee is later restored.
Soft delete only for Employees and Departments – EmployeeTask has IsDeleted for cascade only.
A Department cannot be soft-deleted while it has active employees.
HR creates both the Employee record and the ApplicationUser account in one transaction when adding a new employee.

All business rules enforced in service layer – Controllers only orchestrate HTTP flow. HR-created employee accounts have IsPasswordChangeRequired = true and must change password on first login before accessing any other page. HTTPS is enforced system-wide via HSTS. All list endpoints are paginated (default 20 per page). DepartmentHead cannot approve their own leave; only HR can. DepartmentHead cannot assign tasks to themselves.
Policy classes centralise reusable rules – Services call policies, not the other way around.
Transactions used for all multi-save operations.
A web-based HR Management System for small organizations. Built as an educational ASP.NET Core 10 MVC project with a clean 3-tier architecture and real authentication via ASP.NET Core Identity.
Authentication: login/logout, Remember Me, Forgot Password.
Manage employees (CRUD, soft delete) – HR only. Account creation is part of employee creation.
View employees (all by HR, own department by DepartmentHead, own profile by everyone).
Assign tasks – Only DepartmentHeads to their own department members.
Update task status – Only the assigned employee.
Process payroll (monthly, with itemised bonuses/deductions) – HR only.
View payrolls (all by HR, department by DepartmentHead, own by Employee).
Request leave (all employees) – With balance validation (Annual, Sick, Unpaid).
Approve/reject leave requests – HR (all) or DepartmentHead (own department, excluding their own requests).
View attendance reports (all by HR, department by DepartmentHead, own by Employee).
Email notifications (Forgot Password uses on-screen token for educational purposes – see Section 11).
HR can create, edit, soft-delete departments.
HR can create, edit, soft-delete employees. Creating an employee also creates an ApplicationUser and assigns the correct Identity role — all in one transaction.
Each department must have exactly one manager (non-HR, active, same department, holds DepartmentHead role).
HR cannot delete an employee who is a department manager unless replaced first.
DepartmentHeads can assign tasks to employees in their own department.
Only the assigned employee can update a task's status (Pending → InProgress → Completed).
HR can process monthly payroll for any employee, adding multiple bonus/deduction items.
Payroll NetSalary = BaseSalary + sum(Bonuses) – sum(Deductions), computed by service.
Payroll status flows: Draft → Approved → Paid (no reversal).
Employees can request leave (Annual, Sick, Unpaid) with balance validation (except Unpaid).
Leave requests cannot overlap approved leaves for the same employee.
HR or DepartmentHead can approve/reject leave requests (DepartmentHead only for own department). A DepartmentHead cannot approve or reject their own leave request — those must be handled by HR.
Approved leave increments the employee's UsedDays in LeaveBalances.
Employees can check in/out daily; one record per day; check-out only after check-in.
DepartmentHead can mark attendance for all employees in their own department.
When an employee is soft-deleted, all tasks where AssignedById = employeeId OR AssignedToId = employeeId are also soft-deleted in the same transaction. Silent cascade. Not reversed on restore.
A department cannot be soft-deleted if it has active employees.
Users authenticate via email + password. Login supports Remember Me. Forgot Password flow generates a reset token displayed on-screen.
Manager replacement is a single transaction: update Department.ManagerId, remove DepartmentHead role from old manager, add DepartmentHead role to new manager.
All timestamps stored as UTC, displayed in local time.
Business rule violations must show friendly error messages (no raw exceptions).
Soft-deleted records excluded from all main lists but restorable via separate view.
Authorized pages enforce role checks via [Authorize(Roles=...)] on base controllers.
HTTPS enforced via HSTS in Program.cs (UseHttpsRedirection + UseHsts). All HTTP requests are redirected to HTTPS.
All list views must be paginated with a default page size of 20 records per page. Page size must be configurable.
UI must meet WCAG 2.1 Level A accessibility compliance. All form inputs require associated labels; images require alt attributes.

Critical Rule — DepartmentHead Must Stay in Sync
The DepartmentHead Identity role and Department.ManagerId are two representations of the same fact.
They MUST always match. Any operation that changes one must change the other in the same transaction:
• ReplaceManagerAsync: remove DeptHead role from old manager, add to new manager, update ManagerId.
• SoftDeleteEmployee: if employee is a manager, block deletion (force replacement first).
• CreateEmployee: if assigned DepartmentHead role, also set Department.ManagerId.
HR fills out the Create Employee form: name, email, department, salary, hire date, role (HR / DepartmentHead / Employee), initial password.
Employee record is created and saved (gets auto-generated Id).
ApplicationUser is created via UserManager: Email = employee.Email, UserName = employee.Email, EmployeeId = employee.Id.
Initial password is set via UserManager.AddPasswordAsync().
Identity role is assigned via UserManager.AddToRoleAsync().
If role is DepartmentHead: Department.ManagerId is also updated to this employee's Id.
Transaction commits. On any failure, all changes are rolled back.
Every department must have exactly one manager at all times.
The manager must satisfy all four conditions:
The manager's ApplicationUser must hold the DepartmentHead Identity role.
HR cannot delete an employee who is a department manager. Replacement must come first.
1. Validate the new manager (same dept, active, non-HR, non-deleted, not current manager).
2. Remove DepartmentHead role from old manager's ApplicationUser (UserManager.RemoveFromRoleAsync).
3. Add DepartmentHead role to new manager's ApplicationUser (UserManager.AddToRoleAsync).
All four steps happen inside BeginTransactionAsync(). If any step fails, all are rolled back.
After this succeeds, HR may optionally delete the original manager (now just an Employee).
SoftDeleteAsync(employeeId) must soft-delete all EmployeeTask rows where AssignedById = employeeId OR AssignedToId = employeeId, in the same transaction as the employee soft-delete.
Silent — no notification raised. No error if the employee had no tasks.
RestoreAsync(employeeId) does NOT restore cascaded tasks. They remain IsDeleted = true.
DepartmentService.SoftDeleteAsync rejects if any Employee with DepartmentId = deptId has IsDeleted = false.
Error message: 'Cannot delete department “{Name}”: it still has {count} active employee(s). Reassign or remove them first.'
Only employees with the DepartmentHead role (checked via User.IsInRole or service) can assign tasks.
Tasks can only be assigned to employees in the same department (TaskAssignmentPolicy).
Status: Pending → InProgress → Completed only. No regression.
Only the assignee (AssignedToId) can update status.

Only the creator (AssignedById) can edit details — only if Status != Completed. A DepartmentHead cannot assign a task to themselves (TaskAssignmentPolicy: AssignedById != AssignedToId). A task is considered overdue when DueDate IS NOT NULL AND DueDate < GETUTCDATE() AND Status != Completed. Overdue tasks are highlighted in the dashboard.
UNIQUE (EmployeeId, Month, Year) — one payroll per employee per month.
BaseSalary is a snapshot; NetSalary = BaseSalary + TotalBonus – TotalDeduction.
Status: Draft → Approved → Paid (no reversal, no editing after Approved).
EndDate ≥ StartDate. No overlapping approved leaves. A DepartmentHead cannot approve or reject their own leave request — only HR can action their requests.
Balance checked before submission for Annual/Sick. Unpaid: no limit, no balance row.
On approval: UsedDays += calendar days. On rejection of approved leave: UsedDays -= days.
Auto-create balance row for future years (Annual=20, Sick=10).
UNIQUE (EmployeeId, Date). IsPresent derived from CheckInTime IS NOT NULL.
No double check-in. Check-out requires prior check-in. CheckOut > CheckIn.

✅ Valid email + password — login succeeds, redirected to /Employee.
✅ Wrong password — login fails with error. After 5 attempts: account locked.
✅ Remember Me checked — auth cookie persists beyond session.
✅ Remember Me unchecked — cookie expires with browser session.
✅ Forgot Password with valid email — reset link shown on screen.
✅ Forgot Password with unknown email — same generic success message (no user enumeration).
✅ Reset Password with valid token — password changed, redirect to login.
✅ Reset Password with expired/invalid token — rejected with error.
✅ HR creates employee — Employee record + ApplicationUser + role created in one transaction.
✅ New employee can log in with the password set by HR.
✅ Duplicate email — rejected at both Employee and Identity level.
✅ Creating a DepartmentHead employee — Department.ManagerId updated in same transaction.
✅ Soft-delete employee who is NOT a manager — tasks cascade-deleted (both FK directions).
✅ Soft-delete employee who IS a manager — blocked, link to Replace Manager.
✅ Restore soft-deleted employee — back in active list; tasks remain deleted.
✅ Replace manager — old manager loses DepartmentHead role; new manager gains it; Department.ManagerId updated; all in one transaction.
✅ After replacement, old manager can log in but no longer sees DeptHead-only pages.
✅ New manager can immediately see and use DeptHead-only features.
✅ Replace with invalid employee (different dept, HR, inactive) — rejected.
✅ Any failure mid-transaction — all changes rolled back; roles and ManagerId unchanged.
✅ Create dept with valid manager — succeeds.
✅ Soft-delete dept with active employees — blocked (FR17).
✅ Soft-delete dept after employees removed — succeeds.
✅ DeptHead assigns task to own dept employee — succeeds.
✅ DeptHead assigns task to different dept employee — rejected.
✅ HR tries to assign task — rejected.
✅ Employee updates own task: Pending → InProgress → Completed — succeeds.
✅ Update task assigned to someone else — rejected.
✅ HR processes payroll — record + items created; NetSalary correct.
✅ Draft → Approved → Paid transitions — all succeed.
✅ Employee views own payslip with itemised breakdown.
✅ DeptHead approves own dept leave — UsedDays increments.
✅ DeptHead approves other dept leave — rejected.
✅ Unpaid leave — no balance check, no row touched.
✅ DeptHead marks other dept attendance — rejected.
✅ Soft-delete employee with created tasks — AssignedById tasks → IsDeleted = true.
✅ Soft-delete employee with assigned tasks — AssignedToId tasks → IsDeleted = true.
✅ Soft-delete with both created + assigned tasks — all deleted, no duplicates.
✅ Soft-delete with no tasks — no side effects, transaction commits.
✅ Restore employee — tasks remain IsDeleted = true.
✅ Task lists never show IsDeleted = true tasks.
